answer.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both declining 4-6% QoQ. Durable memory shows that shortening onboarding (memory_86) and signup simplification (memory_31) both reliably lifted adoption and activation. Activation messaging (memory_91) provides additional mechanism. These are proven levers with sustainable payoff that directly address both current metrics. We verify the two core onboarding experiments to confirm their effect sizes and confirm no hidden retention cost before scaling. Promotional pricing is rejected: memory_73 explicitly warns it materially reduces 30-day retention and should not generalize—exactly wrong for sustainable long-term revenue. Referral incentives suit existing customers (memory_57), not the current activation gap. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is valuable but won't move the SMB activation needle this week. A small guarded test on simplified onboarding lets us confirm replication under current conditions before broader rollout.
